ciborium.context: Lidded cup on a tall stem with a small cross on its domed lid, used in churches to hold the consecrated hosts. Useful for Mass, Holy Communion and liturgy resources.

prayer-kneeler.context: Side view of a prie-dieu, a small prayer desk with a padded kneeling step and a slanted armrest. Used for private prayer, chapels and church furniture.

confessional-booth.context: Wooden confessional booth with a curtained middle bay between two doors and a cross on its peaked top. Used for confession times, the sacrament of reconciliation and church services.

scapular.context: Two small cloth panels joined by cord loops and worn over the shoulders, one panel marked with a cross. A Catholic devotional item used in parish shops and devotion guides.

saint-medal.context: Oval religious medal showing a haloed robed figure, hanging from a small ring. Used for patron saint medals, devotional jewellery and church gift shops.

orthodox-icon.context: Framed panel painting of a haloed figure shown head and shoulders, in the style of Byzantine and Orthodox icons. Used for icon painting, Orthodox churches and religious art.

iconostasis.context: Church screen wall with a row of icon panels over two side doors and an arched central door. Found in Eastern Orthodox and Eastern Catholic churches between the nave and the sanctuary.

forehead-ashes.context: Head in profile with a small ash cross marked on the forehead. Used for Ash Wednesday, the start of Lent and church service schedules.

hymnal.context: Closed hymn book with a music note on its cover and a ribbon bookmark. Used for hymns, church music, choirs and worship service orders.

coptic-cross.context: Equal-armed cross with flared arms ending in three rounded points around a central ring. Associated with the Coptic Orthodox Church of Egypt and Ethiopian Christianity.

tau-cross.context: T-shaped cross with a flat top bar flaring at its ends and no upper arm. Associated with Saint Francis, the Franciscans and Saint Anthony.

patriarchal-cross.context: Upright cross with two crossbars, the upper one shorter than the lower. Used as the archiepiscopal cross and in Orthodox and Eastern European heraldry.

khachkar.context: Round-topped stone slab carved with a budding cross above a small rosette. Khachkars are Armenian cross stones used as memorials and at churches.

reliquary.context: Small house-shaped casket with a peaked roof topped by a cross, standing on short feet. A reliquary holds relics of saints and appears in church treasuries and museum collections.

sanctus-bells.context: Cluster of small bells hanging from a crossbar held by a short handle. Rung at the altar during Mass at the consecration.

cross-necklace.context: Chain necklace hanging in a V with a small cross pendant. Used for Christian jewellery, gifts, baptism and confirmation.

calvary-crosses.context: Three crosses standing on a rounded hill, the middle one taller than the two beside it. Represents Calvary and the crucifixion, used for Good Friday and Easter.

cherub.context: Round child's face with curly hair and small wings spreading from behind the head. Used for cherubs and putti in art, Christmas and Valentine decoration and heaven themes.

angel-wings.context: Pair of feathered wings spread wide with a halo floating between them. Used for angels, memorials, remembrance, heaven and guardian angel themes.

altar-cruets.context: Two small jugs with stoppers and handles standing on a tray, holding the wine and water for Mass. Used for liturgy, altar servers and church supplies.

prosphora.context: Round loaf of bread seen from above, stamped with a square seal divided by a cross into four parts. Prosphora is the communion bread of the Orthodox Church.

semantron.context: Long wooden plank held at its waist and struck with a small mallet to call people to prayer. Used in Orthodox monasteries such as Mount Athos.

ihs-christogram.context: The letters IHS under a small cross inside a ring of short rays. The IHS christogram is a monogram of the name of Jesus used by the Jesuits and on church decoration.

anchor-cross.context: Mariner's cross: a cross whose foot ends in the curved flukes of an anchor. An early Christian symbol of hope, also used for sailors and Saint Clement.

easter-lily.context: Two trumpet-shaped lily flowers on one stem with long narrow leaves. Used for Easter, spring services, church decoration and resurrection themes.

sanctuary-lamp.context: Hanging oil lamp with a flame in a cup held by a metal holder on chains. The sanctuary lamp burns near the tabernacle in churches.

galero-hat.context: Wide flat-brimmed hat with cords ending in rows of tassels on both sides. The galero appears in church heraldry above the arms of cardinals and bishops.

biretta.context: Square clerical cap with curved fins on top and a pompom in the centre. Worn by Catholic and Anglican clergy.

papal-tiara.context: Beehive-shaped triple crown with a small cross on top and two ribbons hanging behind. The papal tiara is a symbol of the papacy used in heraldry and history.

crossed-keys.context: Two keys crossed in an X with their bits at the top. The keys of heaven are a symbol of Saint Peter, the papacy and the Holy See.

rose-cross.context: Latin cross with a five-petal rose blooming where the bars meet. The rose cross is associated with Rosicrucianism and Western esoteric traditions.

grotto-shrine.context: Rocky cave arch sheltering a small haloed statue with candles at its base. Used for Marian grottoes, Lourdes-style shrines and pilgrimage sites.

easter-basket.context: Woven basket with an arched handle holding three decorated eggs. Used for Easter, egg hunts, spring holidays and gifts.

gothic-cathedral.context: Cathedral front with two spired towers, a round rose window and a pointed doorway. Used for cathedrals, gothic architecture, cities and church landmarks on maps.

basilica.context: Columned church front with a triangular pediment and a large dome with a cross behind. Used for basilicas, domed churches and church landmarks on maps.

monastery.context: Walled monastery with a bell tower, a long roofed hall and an arched gateway. Used for monasteries, abbeys, convents, retreats and religious communities.

catacomb.context: Arched underground tunnel receding into the distance with burial niches in its walls. Used for catacombs, crypts, early Christian history and underground tours.

western-wall.context: Wall of large stone blocks with a plant growing from a joint and paper notes tucked into the cracks. Represents the Western Wall in Jerusalem, a holy site for Jewish prayer.

river-ghat.context: Stone steps descending to rippling water with a small spired shrine at the top. Ghats are riverside steps used for bathing, rituals and ceremonies in India.

prayer-room.context: Sign showing a doorway with a kneeling figure holding folded hands. Marks prayer rooms, multifaith rooms and quiet rooms in airports, hospitals, universities and offices.

fire-temple.context: Columned temple on a stepped base with a large flame rising above its roof. Represents a Zoroastrian fire temple where a sacred fire is kept burning.

bodhi-tree.context: Broad spreading tree with a thick trunk and heart-shaped leaves with long tips. The Bodhi tree is the sacred fig under which the Buddha attained enlightenment.

shinto-sacred-tree.context: Old tree with a thick trunk girded by a straw rope hung with zigzag paper streamers. Sacred trees like this stand at Shinto shrines in Japan.

noahs-ark.context: Wooden ark with a cabin on deck floating on a wave under a rainbow. Represents Noah's Ark from the flood story, used for Sunday school and children's Bible material.

burning-bush.context: Small rounded bush with flames rising from it. Represents the burning bush of the Moses story in Exodus.

loaves-and-fishes.context: Basket holding two round loaves above two fish. Represents the miracle of the loaves and fishes, the feeding of the five thousand.

tower-of-babel.context: Tall tapering tower with a ramp spiralling up to an unfinished top. Represents the Tower of Babel from Genesis, and themes of languages and ambition.

ark-of-the-covenant.context: Chest on carrying poles with two winged figures facing each other on its lid. Represents the Ark of the Covenant that held the tablets of the Ten Commandments.

pearly-gates.context: Arched double gate studded with pearls, standing on clouds with rays behind. Represents the gates of heaven, used for afterlife, memorial and heaven themes.

ladder-to-heaven.context: Tall ladder rising from the ground into a cloud with rays of light. Represents Jacob's ladder and the idea of a stairway to heaven.

forbidden-fruit.context: Apple with a leaf and a small snake coiled around its stem with its head raised. Represents the forbidden fruit and the serpent in the Garden of Eden.

parting-sea.context: Two towering walls of water curling on either side of a dry path. Represents the parting of the Red Sea in the Exodus story.

torah-crown.context: Domed crown with a band, curved ribs meeting at a finial and small bells on its rim. The keter placed over a Torah scroll in the synagogue.

torah-finials.context: Pair of Torah finials: stems topped by pomegranate-shaped knobs hung with little bells. Rimonim are placed on the rollers of a Torah scroll.

chai-symbol.context: The Hebrew word chai, meaning life, written with the letters chet and yud. A popular Jewish emblem on pendants, gifts and toasts.

hanukkah-gelt.context: Small mesh bag tied at the top with round chocolate coins spilling out. Gelt is given to children at Hanukkah and used for dreidel games.

memorial-candle.context: Lit candle burning inside a glass tumbler. Used for yahrzeit and remembrance candles, mourning, memorial days and vigils.

priestly-breastplate.context: Square breastplate set with twelve gems in four rows of three, hung from two chains. The hoshen worn by the High Priest, one stone for each tribe of Israel.

wudu-station.context: Row of taps above a long washing trough with low stools in front. Marks wudu or ablution areas at mosques, airports and prayer rooms for washing before prayer.

prostration-prayer.context: Figure in prostration on a prayer mat with forehead and palms on the ground. Represents sujood in Muslim prayer and prayer times.

attar-bottle.context: Small round cut-glass perfume bottle with a long thin stopper. Used for attar and oud perfume oils, fragrance shops and gifts.

call-to-prayer.context: Slender minaret with a balcony and a loudspeaker sending out sound waves. Represents the adhan, the Muslim call to prayer, and prayer time alerts.

moon-sighting.context: Telescope on a tripod pointed up at a thin crescent moon. Represents sighting the new crescent moon to start Ramadan, Eid and Islamic months.

iftar-meal.context: Bowl of dates beside a glass of water under a thin crescent moon. Represents iftar, the meal that breaks the fast at sunset during Ramadan.

tilak-mark.context: Face with a U-shaped tilak mark on the forehead and a dot below it. Tilak and bindi marks are worn in Hindu worship and ceremonies.

kamandalu.context: Round water pot with a spout on one side and an arched handle over the top. The kamandalu is carried by ascetics and appears in Hindu iconography.

paduka-sandals.context: Pair of flat wooden sandals seen from above, each with a knob post at the toe. Paduka are worn by sages and venerated in Hindu and Jain tradition.

floating-flower-bowl.context: Shallow bowl of water with flower heads and a small candle floating on it. Used for urli bowls, Diwali decoration, offerings and home decor.

vel-spear.context: Tall staff topped by a broad leaf-shaped spear blade. The vel is the divine spear of Murugan, used in Tamil Hindu worship and festivals such as Thaipusam.

vedic-birth-chart.context: Square horoscope chart divided by both diagonals and an inner diamond into twelve houses. The North Indian style chart used in Vedic astrology.

shivling.context: Rounded upright stone marked with three lines, set in a wide base with a spout. The Shiva lingam is worshipped in Shiva temples and at Maha Shivaratri.
